title: Causative
use_hint: Fix the sentence · Enter = check · Enter = next
note: B2 grammar unit, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane, replacing the empty shell. 28 items, inside the 24-40 band. Sits on the passives thread, immediately after b2_passives_advanced, and shares its logic: the subject arranges the action, somebody else performs it. Two blocks split the two things a student gets wrong. The FORM block (12) gaps the past participle with a lemma cue (B11) — *She had her car ____ last week. (repair)* — and its distractors are the other forms of the same lemma (B6): repair / repairing / to repair, with the irregulars (took vs taken, wrote vs written) carrying their own trap. The AUXILIARY block (10) gaps have/get/having/had, so the student meets the pattern across tenses, after modals and after *to*, rather than only in the past. WORD ORDER is the real error and it is deliberately NOT a gap: a cloze cannot test order (E8 territory), so it drives the Use stage instead, where five of six items contrast *had my hair cut* with *had cut my hair* — two grammatical English sentences with completely different meanings, which is exactly the failure G4 warns about and the reason this had to be error-correction rather than a gap. The adversity use (*had his passport stolen*, *had their house broken into*) is taught alongside, because Czech expresses it with a plain active and learners produce the wrong voice. A8 accepts generated as a contraction closure; D1 every item explains its own form. gap_class auxiliary on all 22 gap items. KWT-native per FCE-EXERCISES, but that needs a js/ branch which is James-only under P-engine, so Use is ordinary error-correction.

cards.title: Causative
points: You arrange it; somebody else does the work.
The order never changes, and the order carries the meaning.

cards.title: You already know
points: The passive hides the doer. The causative says **you** arranged it.
Both end in a past participle — that part is familiar.

cards.title: have or get
points: **get** is the everyday twin of **have**. The pattern is identical.
It works in every tense, after modals, and after *to*.

rows: We **get** the car serviced every autumn.
I need to **get** my computer fixed.

cards.title: When it is bad news
points: The same shape covers things that happen **to** you, with nobody arranging anything.
Czech says this with a plain active sentence, so the shape is easy to miss.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: Both versions are real English. Only the order says who did the work.

rows: ~~I had cut my hair~~ (you did it)

items.en: I had my hair cut on Friday.
items.cz: V pátek jsem si nechal ostříhat vlasy.
items.gap: I had my hair ____ on Friday. (cut)
accepts: I'd my hair cut on Friday.
I had my hair cut on Friday.
items.explanation: **have** + object + **past participle**. The participle of *cut* does not change: **cut**.
items.explanation_cz: **have** + předmět + **příčestí minulé**. Příčestí od *cut* se nemění: **cut**.

items.en: She had her car repaired last week.
items.cz: Minulý týden si nechala opravit auto.
items.gap: She had her car ____ last week. (repair)
accepts: She'd her car repaired last week.
She had her car repaired last week.
items.explanation: The car did not repair anything — it was repaired. Past participle: **repaired**.
items.explanation_cz: Auto nic neopravilo — bylo opraveno. Příčestí minulé: **repaired**.

items.en: We are having the kitchen painted this month.
items.cz: Tento měsíc si necháváme vymalovat kuchyň.
items.gap: We are having the kitchen ____ this month. (paint)
accepts: We're having the kitchen painted this month.
We are having the kitchen painted this month.
items.explanation: The causative works in any tense; the participle stays **painted**.
items.explanation_cz: Vazba funguje v každém čase; příčestí zůstává **painted**.

items.en: He had his suit cleaned before the wedding.
items.cz: Před svatbou si nechal vyčistit oblek.
items.gap: He had his suit ____ before the wedding. (clean)
accepts: He'd his suit cleaned before the wedding.
He had his suit cleaned before the wedding.
items.explanation: **had** + suit + **cleaned** — somebody else did the cleaning.
items.explanation_cz: **had** + suit + **cleaned** — čistil to někdo jiný.

items.en: They had the photographs taken in the garden.
items.cz: Fotky si nechali udělat na zahradě.
items.gap: They had the photographs ____ in the garden. (take)
accepts: They'd the photographs taken in the garden.
They had the photographs taken in the garden.
items.explanation: Irregular participle: *take* becomes **taken**, never *took*.
items.explanation_cz: Nepravidelné příčestí: z *take* je **taken**, nikdy *took*.

items.en: I must have these shoes mended.
items.cz: Musím si nechat spravit tyhle boty.
items.gap: I must have these shoes ____. (mend)
accepts: I must have these shoes mended.
items.explanation: After a modal the causative keeps its shape: have + object + **mended**.
items.explanation_cz: Po modálním slovese si vazba drží tvar: have + předmět + **mended**.

items.en: She is having her eyes tested tomorrow.
items.cz: Zítra si nechá vyšetřit oči.
items.gap: She is having her eyes ____ tomorrow. (test)
accepts: She's having her eyes tested tomorrow.
She is having her eyes tested tomorrow.
She has having her eyes tested tomorrow.
items.explanation: **tested** — the eyes are what gets acted on.
items.explanation_cz: **tested** — oči jsou to, s čím se něco dělá.

items.en: We had the old tree removed in spring.
items.cz: Na jaře jsme si nechali odstranit ten starý strom.
items.gap: We had the old tree ____ in spring. (remove)
accepts: We'd the old tree removed in spring.
We had the old tree removed in spring.
items.explanation: **removed** — you arranged it, somebody else did it.
items.explanation_cz: **removed** — zařídil jsi to, udělal to někdo jiný.

items.en: He had his passport stolen at the airport.
items.cz: Na letišti mu ukradli pas.
items.gap: He had his passport ____ at the airport. (steal)
accepts: He'd his passport stolen at the airport.
He had his passport stolen at the airport.
items.explanation: Same shape, unhappy meaning: this happened TO him. Participle **stolen**.
items.explanation_cz: Stejný tvar, nepříjemný význam: stalo se to JEMU. Příčestí **stolen**.

items.en: I want to have my teeth checked this year.
items.cz: Letos si chci nechat zkontrolovat zuby.
items.gap: I want to have my teeth ____ this year. (check)
accepts: I want to have my teeth checked this year.
items.explanation: The causative also follows an infinitive: to have + object + **checked**.
items.explanation_cz: Vazba jde i po infinitivu: to have + předmět + **checked**.

items.en: They had the report written by a lawyer.
items.cz: Tu zprávu si nechali napsat od právníka.
items.gap: They had the report ____ by a lawyer. (write)
accepts: They'd the report written by a lawyer.
They had the report written by a lawyer.
items.explanation: Irregular again: **written**. *By a lawyer* names who actually did it.
items.explanation_cz: Zase nepravidelné: **written**. *By a lawyer* říká, kdo to opravdu udělal.

items.en: She had her bag searched at the border.
items.cz: Na hranici jí prohledali tašku.
items.gap: She had her bag ____ at the border. (search)
accepts: She'd her bag searched at the border.
She had her bag searched at the border.
items.explanation: **searched** — again something done to her, not by her.
items.explanation_cz: **searched** — zase něco, co udělali jí, ne ona.

items.en: I had my hair cut on Friday.
items.cz: V pátek jsem si nechal ostříhat vlasy.
items.gap: I ____ my hair cut on Friday.
accepts: I'd my hair cut on Friday.
I had my hair cut on Friday.
items.explanation: Past time, so **had** my hair cut.
items.explanation_cz: Minulý čas, proto **had** my hair cut.

items.en: We get the car serviced every autumn.
items.cz: Auto si necháváme servisovat každý podzim.
items.gap: We ____ the car serviced every autumn.
accepts: We get the car serviced every autumn.
items.explanation: **get** is the everyday twin of *have* here, and *every autumn* makes it present simple.
items.explanation_cz: **get** je tu běžnější dvojče slova *have* a *every autumn* dělá přítomný prostý.

items.en: She is going to have the flat cleaned.
items.cz: Nechá si uklidit byt.
items.gap: She is going to ____ the flat cleaned.
accepts: She's going to have the flat cleaned.
She is going to have the flat cleaned.
She has going to have the flat cleaned.
items.explanation: After *to* comes the bare form: **have** the flat cleaned.
items.explanation_cz: Po *to* je základní tvar: **have** the flat cleaned.

items.en: He got his bike repaired at the shop.
items.cz: Nechal si v obchodě opravit kolo.
items.gap: He ____ his bike repaired at the shop.
accepts: He got his bike repaired at the shop.
items.explanation: Past of *get*: **got** his bike repaired.
items.explanation_cz: Minulý čas od *get*: **got** his bike repaired.

items.en: They are having the roof replaced this week.
items.cz: Tento týden si nechávají vyměnit střechu.
items.gap: They are ____ the roof replaced this week.
accepts: They're having the roof replaced this week.
They are having the roof replaced this week.
items.explanation: Present continuous, so the *-ing* form: **having** the roof replaced.
items.explanation_cz: Přítomný průběhový, proto tvar s *-ing*: **having** the roof replaced.

items.en: I need to get my computer fixed.
items.cz: Potřebuju si nechat spravit počítač.
items.gap: I need to ____ my computer fixed.
accepts: I need to get my computer fixed.
items.explanation: After *to* the bare form again: **get** my computer fixed.
items.explanation_cz: Po *to* zase základní tvar: **get** my computer fixed.

items.en: She has had her passport renewed already.
items.cz: Pas už si nechala obnovit.
items.gap: She has ____ her passport renewed already.
accepts: She's had her passport renewed already.
She is had her passport renewed already.
She has had her passport renewed already.
items.explanation: Present perfect: has + **had** + object + past participle.
items.explanation_cz: Předpřítomný čas: has + **had** + předmět + příčestí minulé.

items.en: We will have the windows measured on Monday.
items.cz: V pondělí si necháme změřit okna.
items.gap: We will ____ the windows measured on Monday.
accepts: We'll have the windows measured on Monday.
We will have the windows measured on Monday.
items.explanation: After *will* the bare form: **have** the windows measured.
items.explanation_cz: Po *will* základní tvar: **have** the windows measured.

items.en: He got his wallet taken on the tram.
items.cz: V tramvaji mu vzali peněženku.
items.gap: He ____ his wallet taken on the tram.
accepts: He got his wallet taken on the tram.
items.explanation: **got** works for the unhappy meaning too — it happened to him.
items.explanation_cz: **got** funguje i pro nepříjemný význam — stalo se to jemu.

items.en: They had their house broken into last year.
items.cz: Loni se jim vloupali do domu.
items.gap: They ____ their house broken into last year.
accepts: They'd their house broken into last year.
They had their house broken into last year.
items.explanation: **had** their house broken into — the classic bad-news causative.
items.explanation_cz: **had** their house broken into — klasická vazba pro špatnou zprávu.

items.en: I had my hair cut on Friday.
items.cz: V pátek jsem si nechal ostříhat vlasy.
items.wrong: I had cut my hair on Friday.
accepts: I'd my hair cut on Friday.
I had my hair cut on Friday.
items.explanation: Word order carries the meaning. **have + hair + cut** means somebody cut it for you; *had cut my hair* means you did it yourself.
items.explanation_cz: Slovosled nese význam. **have + hair + cut** znamená, že to udělal někdo jiný; *had cut my hair* znamená, že jsi to udělal sám.

items.en: She had her car repaired last week.
items.cz: Minulý týden si nechala opravit auto.
items.wrong: She had repaired her car last week.
accepts: She'd her car repaired last week.
She had her car repaired last week.
items.explanation: Object before the participle: **her car repaired**, not *repaired her car*.
items.explanation_cz: Předmět před příčestím: **her car repaired**, ne *repaired her car*.

items.en: They had the photographs taken in the garden.
items.cz: Fotky si nechali udělat na zahradě.
items.wrong: They had the photographs took in the garden.
accepts: They'd the photographs taken in the garden.
They had the photographs taken in the garden.
items.explanation: The causative needs the **past participle**: *taken*, not *took*.
items.explanation_cz: Vazba potřebuje **příčestí minulé**: *taken*, ne *took*.

items.en: I need to get my computer fixed.
items.cz: Potřebuju si nechat spravit počítač.
items.wrong: I need to get fixed my computer.
accepts: I need to get my computer fixed.
items.explanation: The object comes first: get **my computer fixed**.
items.explanation_cz: Předmět je první: get **my computer fixed**.

items.en: We are having the kitchen painted this month.
items.cz: Tento měsíc si necháváme vymalovat kuchyň.
items.wrong: We are having painted the kitchen this month.
accepts: We're having the kitchen painted this month.
We are having the kitchen painted this month.
items.explanation: Same order every time: having **the kitchen painted**.
items.explanation_cz: Pokaždé stejné pořadí: having **the kitchen painted**.

items.en: He had his passport stolen at the airport.
items.cz: Na letišti mu ukradli pas.
items.wrong: He had stolen his passport at the airport.
accepts: He'd his passport stolen at the airport.
He had his passport stolen at the airport.
items.explanation: *Had stolen his passport* makes him the thief. **had his passport stolen** is what happened to him.
items.explanation_cz: *Had stolen his passport* z něj dělá zloděje. **had his passport stolen** je to, co se mu stalo.
